# Performance Evidence Checklist: Unified Table Processing and Atomic Transaction Optimization

**Purpose**: Review whether the written Phase H requirements for DML, query, storage, and transaction performance evidence are complete, clear, consistent, and measurable before more implementation. This tests the requirements, not the running benchmarks.
**Created**: 2026-10-31
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), [plan.md](../plan.md) Phase H, [dml-storage-performance-handoff.md](../dml-storage-performance-handoff.md), tasks T069–T089

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are baseline identity fields (source commit, dirty-diff fingerprint, binary fingerprint, toolchain, profile, features, SQL file hashes, server settings, and timestamps) required for every later comparison, not only for the first A1 run? [Completeness, Spec §FR-036, Handoff §A1]
- [ ] CHK002 Are the eight correctness gates written as blocking requirements for every performance slice, including conditional claim, batch-builder, index, tombstone, column-family, and streaming slices? [Completeness, Handoff "Non-negotiable correctness gates", Plan Phase H]
- [ ] CHK003 Is an evidence row required for each shipped slice, naming the finding, the change, the measured outcome, and the remaining issue? [Completeness, Handoff "Objective and boundaries", tasks T069–T089]
- [ ] CHK004 Are USER and SHARED both required in performance acceptance, and is stream participation limited to shared primitives that do not invent a stream transaction model? [Completeness, Spec §FR-035, Handoff "Ownership and shared processing"]
- [ ] CHK005 Are the architecture review-gate outputs (ownership map before the edit; shared entry point, remaining table-specific differences, deleted paths, production-code delta, and any new public interface after it) required for each completed slice? [Completeness, Handoff "Review gate for each completed slice", Plan Phase H]
- [ ] CHK006 Are stage counters for planning, scan/filter, overlay, staging/folding, target resolution, encoding/index construction, backend submission, and post-commit work required in the final evidence, not only in the initial attribution table? [Completeness, Spec §FR-036, Handoff §A1, tasks T089]
- [ ] CHK007 Are new memory budgets or user-facing settings required to be documented before a slice can ship? [Completeness, Spec §FR-037, Handoff "Verification and quantitative acceptance"]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK008 Is "current baseline" defined as the same-profile `dev` suite from T069, with the saved October 27 release timings excluded from regression comparison? [Clarity, Handoff "Baseline and prioritization", Spec Assumptions, tasks T069]
- [ ] CHK009 Are the 20% total-time goal and the 30% combined #8/#11/#12/#13/#15 goal explicitly goals rather than permission to weaken correctness? [Clarity, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance", Spec §SC-009]
- [ ] CHK010 Is "positive median improvement exceeding measured baseline run-to-run spread" given a computation that can be applied to per-script and total medians? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009, Spec §FR-036]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "unaffected" defined so a script whose stage the slice changes cannot use the 5% regression allowance? [Clarity, Spec §SC-009, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "peak tracked transient memory" defined against the ownership-ledger categories, with RSS reported separately and excluded from the 30% tracked-memory goal? [Clarity, Handoff §D3, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK013 Are "material" claim contention and "dominant" unnecessary index churn given decision thresholds that say when B4 and E1 may change design and when they must stay unchanged? [Clarity, Gap, Handoff §B4, Handoff §E1, Spec §FR-031]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "material" instrumentation overhead defined so profiling runs and timing runs are stored as distinct evidence when that overhead is present? [Clarity, Gap, Handoff §A1]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK015 Do Spec §SC-009 and the handoff regression rule state the same activation bound, including whether the bound is 5% of p95/p99, max(5%, 0.005s) of a script median, or both? [Consistency, Spec §SC-009, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK016 Does Spec §SC-015's median and p99 ceiling override the 5% allowance for any Phase H change that touches system-catalog runtime paths? [Consistency, Spec §SC-009, Spec §SC-015]
- [ ] CHK017 Do the handoff's minimum 300-second churn series and Spec §SC-006's three 10-minute runs name distinct workloads that are both required, or one workload? [Consistency, Spec §SC-006, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance", tasks T089]
- [ ] CHK018 Does the handoff ban on silent commit splits agree with Spec §FR-008 for oversized transactions and for bounded processing chunks? [Consistency, Spec §FR-008, Handoff gates 2, Handoff §D3]
- [ ] CHK019 Do Plan Phase H and the handoff architecture rules agree that a faster result still fails when it adds a second parser, a new crate, a parallel fast path, or a facade over two implementations? [Consistency, Plan Phase H, Handoff "Rules for every optimization", Constitution §I]
- [ ] CHK020 Does Spec §FR-031's separate measured-benefit gate for stable primary-key indexes agree with E1 remaining an investigation that cannot ship inside the row-format writer flag? [Consistency, Spec §FR-031, Handoff §E1, tasks T056, tasks T082]
- [ ] CHK021 Does Constitution §I, which allows hot-path complexity only for a measured benefit, agree with the handoff rule that an unmeasured format or layout migration stays unshipped? [Consistency, Constitution §I, Handoff Phase E]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK022 Can a slice be accepted or refused from required evidence fields: baseline, candidate, metric, repeat count, median, range, runtime in seconds, and memory? [Measurability, Spec §FR-036, Constitution §I]
- [ ] CHK023 Can the 16-script protocol be decided as pass or fail from warmup, reset, preserved order, alternated engine order, and a ban on timing a dependent script against arbitrary state? [Measurability, Handoff §A1, tasks T069]
- [ ] CHK024 Can result correctness be decided from checksum or multiset comparison outside the timed section, including NULL, types, duplicate multiplicity, and float tolerance? [Measurability, Handoff §A1]
- [ ] CHK025 Is "at least five matched repeats" specified for the simple-query suite, and is a separate repeat rule specified for the 1/8/32-client workloads and the soak? [Measurability, Spec §SC-009, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK026 Can the program be refused as incomplete when only small allocation fixes exist and the A–D evidence, correctness matrix, and memory acceptance are still open? [Measurability, Handoff "Execution order and reporting", tasks T089, Spec §SC-012]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK027 Are hot-only and mixed hot/cold workloads specified separately, including the rule that the hot-only suite cannot validate the cold-scan copying change? [Coverage, Handoff §C3, Handoff §F2]
- [ ] CHK028 Are prepared-statement concurrency results specified as a separate contract from the one-connection simple-query suite? [Coverage, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK029 Are pinned-snapshot growth and post-unpin reclamation specified as distinct soak outcomes, including which retained growth is expected while a reader is pinned? [Coverage, Handoff §E3, Handoff "Performance and memory acceptance"]
- [ ] CHK030 Are explicit non-implementation outcomes specified for claims, a new batch builder, stable index references, compact tombstones, and column-family grouping when measurement does not justify them? [Coverage, Handoff §B4, Handoff §D2, Handoff Phase E]
- [ ] CHK031 Are concurrent plan coalescing, cold-scan copying, and SELECT streaming specified as evidence-selected extensions rather than mandatory wins on the single-connection hot-only suite? [Coverage, Handoff "Additional improvements"]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK032 Are requirements defined for a missed numeric goal, so the report names the remaining bottleneck instead of marking the program complete? [Edge Case, Handoff "Execution order and reporting", tasks T089]
- [ ] CHK033 Are requirements defined so a large single row cannot satisfy a row-count-only memory bound, and so scans beyond 100,000 raw rows complete or fail explicitly? [Edge Case, Handoff §C1, Handoff §C3]
- [ ] CHK034 Are requirements defined for missing or stale statistics, including a conservative access choice that does not scan the table on every request? [Edge Case, Handoff §D1]
- [ ] CHK035 Are requirements defined for a slow client, an error after partial SELECT delivery, disconnect, and DML `RETURNING` that must not publish ahead of its commit boundary? [Edge Case, Handoff §F3]
- [ ] CHK036 Are allocator-cache and RocksDB retention distinguished from the requirement that logical live bytes return to baseline after cleanup? [Edge Case, Handoff §D3]
- [ ] CHK037 Are requirements defined so a durability, cache, or profile change cannot be reported as a speedup against a mismatched baseline? [Edge Case, Spec Assumptions, Handoff §A1]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK038 Is the measurement order specified so the current baseline exists before later slices, write-set consumption is measured before one-decode preparation, and admission plumbing exists before streaming expansion? [Dependency, Plan Phase H, Handoff "Execution order and reporting"]
- [ ] CHK039 Is it specified that evidence-gated index, tombstone, and column-family investigations do not block shipping the earlier DML, query, and storage slices? [Dependency, Handoff Phase E, tasks Phase 15 checkpoint]
- [ ] CHK040 Does Spec §SC-012 keep checklist completion out of performance acceptance, so this list cannot be cited as proof that a runtime goal was met? [Assumption, Spec §SC-012]

## Notes

- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
